page: Microsoft Azure E4-2s_v5 is a constrained-vCPU, memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. Based on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, featuring 48 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance provisions 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 hyperthreads, coupled with 32.0 GB of memory. This produces an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects the constrained compute topology alongside balanced memory access. Single-threaded performance sits comfortably in the middle tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1627.0 and stress-ng single-core output of 1889.49. In contrast, multi-core metrics place in the bottom 10 percent of evaluated instances, showing a Geekbench multi-core score of 1881.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2980.96 due to the allocation of only two execution threads. Potentially uncached memory bandwidth registers at 14.54 GB/sec for reads and 13.5 GB/sec for writes.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the E4-2s_v5 allows systems to utilize the generous 32.0 GB memory capacity without paying software licensing costs that scale by active processor cores. The primary operational tradeoff is constrained compute density, meaning heavy parallel compute tasks will be throttled by the two-thread limit. The instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads that require lower CPU capability, including small in-memory caches, lightweight database engines, staging environments, and memory-heavy microservices.
